about.title: Hercules Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products don't announce themselves — a faulty ladder, a malfunctioning appliance, a car part that fails near the I-80/SR-4 interchange, or medicine with an inadequate warning label can all cause serious harm. Hercules residents who are hurt this way sometimes assume they need to prove the manufacturer was careless, but California generally applies strict liability to these cases. That means the focus is on whether the product itself was defective in design, manufacture, or warning, and whether that defect caused the injury. Companies up and down the supply chain — makers, distributors, and sellers — may share responsibility. Because Contra Costa County sees its share of injury collisions tied to vehicle parts and equipment failures, product defects sometimes overlap with crash cases too. We handle product liability claims and can evaluate what happened, help preserve the product as evidence, and explain the options available under California law.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Path Forward
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, the case can center on the product's condition rather than requiring proof the manufacturer was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may open more than one avenue for pursuing a claim.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: Our team can advise on keeping the product intact and documented, since the item itself is often central evidence in a defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law frequently relies on strict liability, meaning the focus is typically on whether the product was defective and caused harm, not on proving carelessness. We can review your situation to explain how this applies to your specific claim.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including any packaging, instructions, or parts. This preservation can matter a great deal, since the product is often central evidence in a defect case.

items.question: Are defective product injuries common around Hercules?
items.answer: Hercules sees regular injury collisions along corridors like I-80, San Pablo Avenue, and SR-4, and some of these incidents involve failed vehicle components or safety equipment. A defect isn't always obvious right away, so it's worth having an attorney look at the details.

items.question: Is there a cost for a case review?
items.answer: No. We offer free consultations, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
